5.0.0.en: 1 Then I turned, and lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and behold a flying roll. 2 And he said unto me, What seest thou? And I answered, I see a flying roll; the length thereof is twenty cubits, and the breadth thereof ten cubits. 3 Then said he unto me, This is the curse that goeth forth over the face of the whole earth: for every one that stealeth shall be cut off as on this side according to it; and every one that sweareth shall be cut off as on that side according to it. 4 I will bring it forth, saith the LORD of hosts, and it shall enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him that sweareth falsely by my name: and it shall remain in the midst of his house, and shall consume it with the timber thereof and the stones thereof.

5.0.1.en: The prophet lifted up his eyes and saw a flying scroll (a sheet), and as it came in the Septuagint, “a flying sickle.”

5.1.0.en: The scroll often signifies the proclamation of judgment (Ezek 2:9-10; Rev 5:1; 10:2). Though the people of God appeared in the previous vision as a lampstand all of gold, bearing the light of Christ with the oil of the Holy Spirit, its joy in this divine work is accompanied by caution against every sin or carelessness. As for its flying, it is because the evil we commit here ascends before God as a corrupt odor, so it pours out a curse “over the face of the whole earth” [3]. Here God declares the responsibility of the believer as a member of the whole human community, interacting either for blessing or for curse. What he does has an effect on the life of all; for because of Joseph the house of Potiphar was blessed and the storehouses of Egypt were blessed, and because of the flight of Jonah the sea was stirred up and many lost their goods.

5.1.1.en: And the wonder is that the prophet sees evil as a sheet flying open, its length twenty cubits and its breadth ten cubits. On the earth it was folded and no one knew its hidden things, but it will not remain so; rather it will be exposed, and all will be able to read it. As for its dimensions, they are proportionate to the dimensions of the tabernacle or the Holy Place, as though what man commits corrupts the holy things of God in him.

5.1.2.en: But in the Septuagint the prophet sees a flying sickle, and as St. Didymus the Blind says: [Since the Judge separates the righteous from the wicked and repays each one according to his deeds, therefore Holy Scripture calls the retributions under which the unjust and the wicked fall sometimes a sword and an arrow (Deut 32:42; 22:23; Isa 34:5; Amos 9:10; Ps 7:12-13; Jer 47:5-6) and sometimes an axe and a sickle... For the trees that bear no good fruit become the object of wrath and punishment (they are struck with the axe and the sickle)... So it is said: “And now also the axe is laid unto the root of the trees: therefore every tree which bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire” (Mt 3:10). Thus the curse comes upon plants of this kind. And thus the sickle is also used to cut down those who bear corrupt fruits, of whom it was said: “For their rock is not as our Rock, even our enemies themselves being judges. For their vine is of the vine of Sodom, and of the fields of Gomorrah: their grapes are grapes of gall, their clusters are bitter: their wine is the poison of dragons, and the cruel venom of asps” (Deut 32:31-33). Thus the evil will is likened to the corrupt vine that bears bad fruit and must be cut with a sharp sickle and its grapes and clusters removed... The prophet sees it as a flying sickle, not an ordinary sickle but, without doubt, a spiritual one... It cuts down “Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted” (Mt 15:13), that is, “it cuts down everything unclean.”

5.1.3.en: St. John Chrysostom comments on this sharp sickle, saying: [Perhaps a man might escape a flying sword, but from a sickle that comes down upon his neck and winds around it like a rope binding it, he cannot escape. And if wings are added to the sickle, what hope of rescue can be found?!]. He also says: [It is flying, indicating the swiftness of the coming of vengeance... As for its length and breadth being many cubits, it means the severity and enormity of the woes. It flies from heaven, meaning the coming of vengeance from the judgment seat on high, and in the form of a sickle for the inevitability of judgment. For just as the sickle that comes upon the neck and takes hold of it does not return empty but cuts off the head, so vengeance will be severe and sure].

5.1.4.en: The prophet continues his speech: “Then said he unto me, This is the curse that goeth forth over the face of the whole earth: for every one that stealeth shall be cut off as on this side according to it; and every one that sweareth shall be cut off as on that side according to it. I will bring it forth, saith the LORD of hosts, and it shall enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him that sweareth falsely by my name: and it shall remain in the midst of his house, and shall consume it with the timber thereof and the stones thereof” [3-4].

5.1.5.en: The Mosaic covenant carried with it a curse that comes upon the disobedient (Deut 27:15-26; 28:15-68); this curse hovers in the air and threatens the inhabitants of the earth who took the covenant and did not keep it but betrayed it. Here two sins are emphasized: theft and false swearing. By the first a man robs his brother and by the second he despises God, as though the two sins include the breaking of the whole Law: the violation of the right of the brethren and of God. Perhaps the commandment concerning not stealing was in the middle of the second tablet, and that concerning not swearing falsely in the middle of the first, meaning that man breaks the two tablets in their depths.

5.1.6.en: Though the curse touches the whole face of the earth, yet as it flies it strikes its arrow at the house of the wrongdoer himself, to lodge there and destroy it, with its timber and its stones; he receives the natural fruit of his work. St. Didymus the Blind says: [This sickle flies and traverses the whole earth swiftly, striking not only the sinners who are on the earth but also those in the air (the demons) and the wicked wherever they are found. It destroys what is in the midst of the house, that is, the heart and the mind, and it shatters what is within man like the sword that cut in two from the middle the judge of Israel who was burning with the passion of adultery with Susanna: “For, behold, the angel of God hath received sentence of God to cut thee in two” (Additions to Dan 13:55), so cutting the adulterer from the middle means the division of his mind. St. John Chrysostom comments on the destruction of the house of the wicked, saying: [His house becomes a heap, so that everyone who passes by it and looks at it and learns the reason avoids imitating him].

5.2.0.en: 5 Then the angel that talked with me went forth, and said unto me, Lift up now thine eyes, and see what is this that goeth forth. 6 And I said, What is it? And he said, This is the ephah that goeth forth. He said moreover, This is their eye through all the earth. 7 And, behold, there was lifted up a talent of lead: and there was a woman sitting in the midst of the ephah. 8 And he said, This is wickedness. And he cast it into the midst of the ephah; and he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof. 9 Then lifted I up mine eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came out two women, and the wind was in their wings; for they had wings like the wings of a stork: and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the heaven. 10 Then said I to the angel that talked with me, Whither do these bear the ephah? 11 And he said unto me, To build it an house in the land of Shinar: and when it is prepared, it shall be established there upon her own base.

5.3.0.en: Again God warns us against sin, for the prophet saw an ephah going forth [6]. The ephah is the largest unit of measure (for measuring) among the Jews, and its going forth means that the standards or measures are not exact, or what we call “lack of discernment.”

5.4.0.en: The prophet saw: “And, behold, there was lifted up a talent of lead: and there was a woman sitting in the midst of the ephah. And he said, This is wickedness. And he cast it into the midst of the ephah; and he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof” [7-8].

5.4.1.en: Sin is likened to the lead that weighs down the soul to bring it down to the depths of the abyss, as it came in the song of Moses the prophet: “They sank as lead in the mighty waters” (Ex 15:10). Origen says: [It was said of the wicked that they sank in the mighty waters... but the saints do not sink but walk on the waters... since there is not in them the weight of sin that they should sink]. And St. Gregory of Nyssa says: [Each one departs according to his condition, so one goes lightly and another plunges into the waters. For virtue is a light thing that floats, and those who live it fly like a cloud and like doves, as Isaiah says (Isa 60:8)... but sin is heavy and sits upon man like lead]. And St. John Chrysostom says: [Nothing gives it wings and lifts it up like the enjoyment of righteousness and virtue].

5.4.2.en: The prophet saw the talent of lead lifted up, that is, sin was exposed before all, so that evil appeared as a woman sitting in the midst of the ephah that goes forth.

5.4.3.en: St. Didymus the Blind comments on the likening of evil, like virtue, to a woman, saying: [It is not strange that Holy Scripture calls the evil conduct and the corrupt thought and the brute force they generate by the name “woman,” as it calls evil here a woman; likewise in the Book of Proverbs it calls folly a woman. This is the text, for the wise man teaches his disciple, saying: “My son, attend unto my wisdom, and bow thine ear to my understanding: that thou mayest regard discretion, and that thy lips may keep knowledge. For the lips of a strange woman drop as an honeycomb, and her mouth is smoother than oil: but her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a twoedged sword. Her feet go down to death; her steps take hold on hell” (Prov 5:1-5). And in the same Book of Proverbs uncleanness is likened to a woman (Prov 7:7-27)... And just as vices are likened to a woman, so also are virtues, and the wise man says of wisdom: “I loved her beauty and took her to live with me” (Wis 8:2)].

5.4.4.en: We return to the vision to find the weight of lead cast into the mouth of the woman, as though sin is often concentrated in the mouth, so man carries a tongue heavy upon the soul, by which he shatters himself and insults others, in contrast to the righteous man of whom it was said: “The tongue of the just is as choice silver” (Prov 10:2). It is as though the wicked man carries in his mouth a tongue of lead that brings out evils, while the righteous man carries a tongue of pure silver that speaks the word of God refined like silver seven times (Ps 12:6).

5.5.0.en: The prophet continues his speech: “And, behold, there came out two women, and the wind was in their wings; and they had wings like the wings of a stork: and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the heaven” [9].

5.5.1.en: The two women are a figure of two vices, perhaps theft and false swearing as in the previous vision, that is, the robbing of the right of the brethren and the right of God. As for his saying: “the wind was in their wings,” that is, their wings are full of wind or spirit, like the spirit of which the Apostle spoke: “the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience” (Eph 2:2), the evil spirit of which the Lord Christ said that when it is cast out of a man it returns, and finding the place from which it was cast out empty of all goodness and swept of everything beautiful, it comes with seven spirits more wicked than itself to dwell in him, so that the last state of that man is worse than the first (Mt 12:35; Lk 11:26).

5.5.2.en: And lest it be thought from the wings that the two women were rising toward heaven, he made clear that their wings were like the wings of a stork and not like the wings of a dove, as St. Didymus the Blind says: [For the stork according to the Law is an unclean bird (Lev 11:19; Deut 14:18) that dwells in the cypress trees (Ps 104:17). It is among the migratory birds (Jer 8:7). The stork is of two kinds: the white, Ciconia alba, spends the winter in central and southern Africa and migrates in the spring in huge numbers to Europe and Palestine and northern Syria. And the black, Ciconia higra, is found in Palestine and is common in the valley of the Dead Sea. The stork feeds on frogs and small reptiles, and if it finds none it seeks carrion and filth. St. Didymus the Blind comments on this, saying that the two women, who represent evil and symbolize Satan or the Antichrist and the speech of the heretics, live beside the graves to feed on carrion, so they are like whited sepulchres, white outwardly, and within full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness (Mt 23:27). And as the stork builds its nest with filth so that its young come forth amid unclean foul odors, so he who walks in evil lives in the empty cares of the flesh. He who has the wings of the stork is drawn to graves and filth, but he who has the wings of a dove, that is, the work of the Holy Spirit who appeared in the form of a dove at the baptism of the Lord, is lifted up to heavenly things, and as St. Didymus the Blind says: [Who is this blessed one who bears the two wings of a dove that lift him to heaven above this world].

5.5.3.en: As for the going of the two women to Shinar [which is associated with Babylon (Gen 10:10)] to build a house for themselves, it signifies their desire to settle in the place where men anciently agreed to rebel against God Himself, so their tongues were confused and they entered into inner turmoil.

5.5.4.en: May we bear the two wings of a dove and not the wings of a stork, so that we flee from Babylon (Isa 48:20), where evil is, to find our rest in the Lord Himself, dwelling in His eternal embrace!

6.0.s.en: 1. The vision of the four chariots:

6.0.0.en: 1 And I turned, and lifted up mine eyes, and looked, and, behold, there came four chariots out from between two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of brass. 2 In the first chariot were red horses; and in the second chariot black horses; 3 and in the third chariot white horses; and in the fourth chariot grisled and bay horses. 4 Then I answered and said unto the angel that talked with me, What are these, my lord? 5 And the angel answered and said unto me, These are the four spirits of the heavens, which go forth from standing before the LORD of all the earth. 6 The black horses which are therein go forth into the north country; and the white go forth after them; and the grisled go forth toward the south country. 7 And the bay went forth, and sought to go that they might walk to and fro through the earth: and he said, Get you hence, walk to and fro through the earth. So they walked to and fro through the earth. 8 Then cried he upon me, and spake unto me, saying, Behold, these that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country.

6.0.1.en: It seems that this vision is an extension of the first vision, which is in chapter one, where he saw the rider on a red horse among the myrtle trees in the shade, and behind him red, bay and white horses; but here he saw “four chariots coming out from between two mountains; and the mountains were mountains of brass. In the first chariot were red horses; and in the second chariot black (dark) horses; and in the third chariot white horses; and in the fourth chariot grisled and bay horses” [1-3].

6.0.2.en: But the first vision signifies God's saving plan by the incarnation of the Word, who comes on a red horse after the rest of the horses have prepared the way for Him, whereas here the vision signifies God's disciplinary plan for evil outside Jerusalem and God's support of the believers against the devil and his wars.

6.1.0.en: He saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains, by which he probably means Mount Moriah and the Mount of Olives, as though the chariots had gone out to the valley of Jehoshaphat, which means: “the valley where Jehovah judges or condemns,” the valley in which the Lord gathers all the nations to judge them there because of their humiliation of His people (Joel 2:3). These four divine chariots, which are “the four spirits of the heavens, which go forth from standing before the LORD of all the earth” [15], have been prepared to carry out God's disciplinary plan outside Jerusalem so that the wicked may not behold the glory of Jerusalem nor enter into it but be disciplined outside, in this world, or be eternally deprived of Jerusalem while the children of God enjoy the inner eternal glory. Perhaps for the same reason the Lord of glory comes to us on the last day on the clouds, so that the wicked do not meet with Him in His glory but see Him fearsome and terrifying, while the righteous enter with Him into the eternal wedding feast.

6.1.1.en: The two mountains surrounding the valley are “mountains of brass” [1], from which no one can escape. It was said of the Lord Christ: “his feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace” (Rev 1:15); he who hides in Him and is united with Him tramples the earth under his feet and its thorns and thistles cannot touch him (Gen 3:18), crushing the curse beneath him in Christ Jesus our Lord. Thus the men of the Old and New Testaments are like two mountains of brass that crush evil in the valley of Jehoshaphat and condemn it by the Lord.

6.1.2.en: St. Didymus the Blind sees that brass signifies the teachings of the sophists and heretics, which are nothing but “sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal” (1 Cor 13:1); they do not have divine love, so there applies to them the saying of the Apostle: “Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, and have not charity, I am become as sounding brass, or a tinkling cymbal.” And as iron signifies rebellion and rigidity, brass signifies hiding error behind appearance, like two mountains of brass—as though it befits us to flee from this valley, the valley of heretics who deceive by their words devoid of true love, lest we come under the fearful judgment of God.

6.1.3.en: As for the colors of the divine chariots, they signify God's disciplines against evil and His help to His people against the devil and his evil works:

6.1.4.en: First: The first chariot with its red horses represents the spiritual wars in which the believer strives against evil unto blood (Zech 12:4), so that evil perishes for the sake of building the inner Kingdom.

6.1.5.en: Second: The second chariot with its black (dark) horses is a sign of the death that the war brings upon the devil and the destruction of his evil works.

6.1.6.en: Third: The third chariot with its white horses follows the preceding chariot, for the death of evil is life for pure virtue. Or, as St. Didymus the Blind sees, the black horses signify the instruments of God's wrath “where evil breaks forth upon all the inhabitants of the land” (Jer 1:14), to be followed by the white horses as a sign of joy after the trial, so the believer says: “Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me. I will bear the indignation of the LORD, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness” (Mic 7:8-9). Thus, when he benefits from the disciplines of the Lord, he praises, saying: “I bless thee, O LORD, for thou hast exercised thine anger upon me for my salvation; thou hast turned back thy face and had mercy upon me” (Isa 12:1).

6.1.7.en: Fourth: The grisled and bay horses coming from the south signify the varied fruit with which the soul overflows within itself by practicing repentance after discipline, for the bride says: “Come, thou south; blow upon my garden, that the spices thereof may flow out” (Song 4:16).

6.1.8.en: These are the four chariots with their horses to which the divine command was given: “Get you hence, walk to and fro through the earth. So they walked to and fro through the earth. Then cried he upon me, and spake unto me, saying, Behold, these that go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country” [7-8]. God in His love sends forth His chariots to work His divine plan in the earth, and when the north country (Babylon), a symbol of the devil, falls under punishment, the Spirit of God is quieted concerning His children. How wonderful! He permitted the north country to be a harsh instrument of discipline for them, yet His Spirit does not settle and His heart does not rest until He sees His people returned to rest in the new Jerusalem, bearing varied fruits and an overflow of blessings without measure. It is as though God who disciplines hears our groaning and groans with our groaning, and does not rest until we rest in Him. We noticed in our study of the Book of Hosea the words of the Lord Himself who permits affliction, saying: “mine heart is turned within me, my repentings are kindled together. I will not execute the fierceness of mine anger, I will not return to destroy Ephraim: for I am God, and not man; the Holy One in the midst of thee: and I will not come in wrath” (Hos 11:8-9).

6.2.s.en: 2. The vision of the crowning of Joshua:

6.2.0.en: 9 And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying, 10 Take of them of the captivity, even of Heldai, of Tobijah, and of Jedaiah, which are come from Babylon, and come thou the same day, and go into the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah; 11 then take silver and gold, and make crowns, and set them upon the head of Joshua the son of Josedech, the high priest; 12 and speak unto him, saying, Thus speaketh the LORD of hosts, saying, Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the LORD: 13 even he shall build the temple of the LORD; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both. 14 And the crowns shall be to Helem, and to Tobijah, and to Jedaiah, and to Hen the son of Zephaniah, for a memorial in the temple of the LORD. 15 And they that are far off shall come and build in the temple of the LORD, and ye shall know that the LORD of hosts hath sent me unto you. And this shall come to pass, if ye will diligently obey the voice of the LORD your God.

6.2.1.en: In chapter three the command was given to take off the filthy garments so that Joshua might put on an adorned garment and a fair mitre (Zech 3:4-5), and in this there was a proclamation of our being crowned in Him; by the Cross He tore up our sins, presenting to us Himself, the mystery of righteousness and victory. But here Joshua is crowned with a crown of silver and gold, and those coming from captivity are crowned with him, as though the aim of this vision is to highlight the crowning of the Church, whose members were formerly under captivity and became citizens of the new Jerusalem. We can say that the first vision signifies the Lord Christ before His Ascension, for He was crowned on the Cross and the Church was crowned in Him, and the second vision signifies the time after the Ascension, for it has become the part of the Church to be crowned by Him and for Christ to be crowned in her inwardly. As St. Augustine said, the Lord Christ was working before the Ascension in the name of the Church hidden in Him and on her behalf, but after the Ascension He hid Himself in her that she might work on His behalf and in His name.

6.2.2.en: Note the following in this vision:

6.2.3.en: First: The name of Joshua was not mentioned among the names of those coming from captivity; he was crowned first, alone, as a type of our Lord Jesus who dwelt among us on our earth without falling under the captivity of sin, nor did the devil find a place for himself in Him. He conquered first and was crowned as the firstborn of those who sleep and ascended to His heavenly house so that by Him and in Him we may enjoy the crown.

6.2.4.en: Second: The Lord asked Zechariah the prophet to take silver and gold from Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah, of the people of the captivity, and make crowns and set them on the head of Joshua the great priest; this silver and gold had previously been seized by the enemy from Jerusalem and the house of the Lord and carried into captivity with the captives to be used for the kingdom of Babylon, and now with the return of the captives the silver and gold are returned to be used in the house of the Lord for the glory of God. It is as though man, when sin takes him captive, has his bodily, psychological and material energies turned to the account of evil, and with his return to the bosom of God he presents all these things to be instruments of righteousness for the glory of God.

6.2.5.en: Third: The names of the men who gather the silver and gold from the captives are:

6.3.0.en: a. Heldai or Cheldai, which means “eternal,” and he is also called “Helem” [14], which means “health” or “strength.”

6.3.2.en: c. “Jedaiah,” which means “Jehovah knows,” and he was the chief of the priests who returned from captivity (Neh 12:6).

6.3.3.en: Thus the three worked together to return to the Lord the silver and gold to be crowns of glory for the Church in her one Bridegroom Joshua. In other words, if our silver and gold are not sanctified, let us look to “eternity,” or the abiding life, that it may give us health of soul and strength of spirit, so that we set out with all our energy to present them as an offering to the Lord. As for the secret of sanctifying these energies, gifts and capabilities, it is the goodness of the Lord and His tenderness, who has compassion on us and accepts our gifts; He knows us as His children and receives us to Himself, so we come to know Him and receive Him in us. In brief, we need to grasp immortality and eternity and to receive the tenderness of God and the knowledge of Him!

6.3.4.en: Fourth: They brought the silver and gold to the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah [10] before turning them into crowns. Since the word “Josiah” means “the one who saves” and the word “Zephaniah” means “Jehovah hides or treasures”; it is as though the sanctification of our energy must be accomplished in the house of “the one who saves,” that is, the Church, the temple of the Lord our Savior, who works in us secretly within the heart, and treasures us like precious jewels prepared for eternal life. God does not want for us the outward appearances that make us lose His splendor in us, but wants for us the hidden glorious life, so that we are counted precious treasures in His eyes!

6.3.5.en: Fifth: When the silver and gold were gathered they became crowns and not one crown, all of them placed on the head of Joshua... as though every crown that a believer enjoys the Bridegroom Himself puts on. Origen says concerning the martyrs that Jesus Christ is the One who calls them to the crown and the One who fights with them and the One who receives it in them. Thus the Lord is manifested in His Church, so He counts every crown of ours as a crown for Himself. And St. Didymus the Blind says: [See how Christ the Great Priest can take upon His head the crowns of all, for all believers represent the body of the Lord Christ and His members, for it was truly said to those who make up the assembly of the Church: “Now ye are the body of Christ, and members in particular” (1 Cor 12:27); among these members some are active hands; and others “not slothful in business” (Rom 12:11) are the feet; and others who have a pure mind are the eyes; and some who govern well and fulfill their responsibility as they should represent the head symbolically... Therefore it is reasonable that the head of the Great Priest should receive all the crowns].

6.3.6.en: St. Didymus the Blind has another interpretation of these many crowns placed on the head of the Lord Christ, saying: [Consider how Jesus alone takes many crowns, for He fought all the wars to the end, “was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin” (Heb 4:15)].

6.3.7.en: Sixth: These crowns that were placed on the head of our Bridegroom alone He presents to us, so He gives each one crowns of many virtues, and as St. Didymus the Blind says: [It is not strange that many crowns be placed on one head, for every virtue has its crown, or rather every virtue is in itself a crown, and the perfect man possesses many crowns... as long as the virtues are bound together, he who possesses them is adorned with many crowns].

6.3.8.en: Seventh: The material of the crowns is silver and gold; silver signifies the word of God (Ps 12:6) and gold the Spirit or the heavenly life, as though it befits us to prepare ourselves for these crowns through the word of God working in us and the heavenly spiritual thought.

6.3.9.en: Eighth: What is the crown that we wear in its essence but a meeting with the Lord Himself, as was said by Isaiah the prophet: “In that day shall the LORD of hosts be for a crown of glory, and for a diadem of beauty” (Isa 28:5), and as St. Didymus the Blind says: [The Lord Himself is the reward of glory, granted to those who glorify God in their bodies (1 Cor 6:20), who have the spirit of submission to the preserved opinions (of the Church) and the pious traditions].

6.3.10.en: Ninth: The Lord Christ is called in this vision the man and the Branch and the East at the same time, for in the Septuagint it was said: “Behold the man, the Branch, the East is his name.” We have previously spoken of these titles in chapter three. The following is the comment of St. Didymus the Blind on this phrase: [Thus saith the LORD of hosts: Behold the man, the Branch, the East is his name, relates to our Savior who comes into this world, for He is the man as the Son of Mary... but He is the true light and the Sun of Righteousness (the East). In agreement with this text Jeremiah says: “Behold, the days come, saith the LORD, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth. In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS” (Jer 23:5-6). Truly He is the Branch of righteousness that springs from David... This Branch is the Sun of Righteousness and has risen from David, He who was born of the land of David according to the flesh (Rom 1:3), as was said by Isaiah the prophet: “And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious” (Isa 10:11)... “Behold the man...”.

6.3.11.en: Here He declares the Bridegroom to whom the bride belongs, so He calls Him “the man.” This is what the Apostle shows when he writes to the Corinthians: “For I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ” (2 Cor 11:2)... Of this man John the Baptist, the greatest of those born of women (Mt 11:11), bears witness, saying: “After me cometh a man which is preferred before me: for he was before me” (Jn 1:30), and he declared this man by saying: “He that hath the bride is the bridegroom: but the friend of the bridegroom, which standeth and heareth him, rejoiceth greatly because of the bridegroom's voice” (Jn 3:29). This One whom the prophet shows to be “the Branch”... He is the Branch from on high, a branch of the true light, the Sun of Righteousness (Mal 4:2), who has risen for those who were in darkness and the shadow of death (Lk 1:78) to dispel the darkness and remove death so that we pass over into life (Jn 5:24). Thus we become light in the Lord, as it is written: “For ye were sometimes darkness, but now are ye light in the Lord” (Eph 5:8).

6.3.12.en: Origen comments on His being called “the East,” saying that the east is of two kinds: a true east that shines upon us, He who says: “I am the light of the world,” and a misleading east like the light of the wicked which is put out (Job 18:5). And like the light of deceitful Satan who appears in the likeness of an angel of light (2 Cor 11:4).

6.3.13.en: Tenth: It was said of the Lord Christ, “and he shall grow up out of his place” [12]; if for our sake He became the Branch, He grows up, giving us true life. As the psalmist says: “Truth shall spring out of the earth” (Ps 85:11). He came to our earth, He who is the Truth able to carry us in Him, so He lifts us from the earth and establishes in us His heavenly house, therefore He continues the saying: “and he shall build the temple of the LORD,” repeating this phrase twice, on the one hand because the number 2, as we said before, signifies “love,” so by love He lifts us from the earth and establishes us as a heavenly house and a living temple for Him, and on the other hand it declares His work with the Jews as with the Gentiles, establishing all together.

6.3.14.en: Eleventh: The temple that He builds here of believers, whether of Jewish or of Gentile origin, He sits in as king and priest at the same time, which was not possible in the temple of Solomon nor in the temple that Zerubbabel built, for the kings were of the tribe of Judah and the priests of the tribe of Levi, but in the new temple the Lord dwelt to reign over us and to be priest on our behalf. “And he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both” [13]. By His kingdom and priesthood He crushes the devil and gives peace to His people. St. Didymus the Blind says: [It is a double throne: the throne of the kingdom and the throne of the priesthood also... an all-powerful throne as it is written in Proverbs: “A king that sitteth in the throne of judgment scattereth away all evil with his eyes” (Prov 20:8), and also: “Thy throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre” (Ps 44:7; Heb 1:8), “The LORD sitteth king” (Ps 29:10). As for the priestly throne, it is written in the Epistle to the Hebrews: “For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless” (Heb 7:26) and also: “Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need” (Heb 4:16). What he calls “the throne of grace” is the throne of the holy, righteous priest without defilement. Therefore he means that He took the throne of His father David to reign forever, and of His kingdom there shall be no end (Lk 1:33), and at the same time His priesthood does not pass away (Heb 7:24)... so He rules on the double throne; He is the only One who has the throne of kingship and priesthood together].

6.3.15.en: Twelfth: He speaks of the crowns that these chiefs enjoy, that they shall be “for a memorial in the temple of the LORD” [14], and in the Septuagint he says: “they shall obtain a song in the temple of the Lord.” For victory by our Lord Jesus Christ generates in us the nature of inner praise and joy of the Spirit, so that all our life turns into a hymn of praise. St. Didymus the Blind says: [We offer the teachings of good works as a hymn of praise that we chant, and delightful thoughts rise up in us like one who strikes the lute and the tambourine. We play on the lute by receiving the teachings of asceticism: “Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth; fornication, uncleanness, inordinate affection, evil concupiscence” (Col 3:5), “Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus” (2 Cor 4:10), through which man becomes rejected and a slave, so that he is like the tambourine made of the skin of dead animals. With this tambourine the five wise virgins who bear shining lamps strike, as in the saying of the psalm: “The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels” (Ps 68:25). These timbrels which the Hebrew women used after the exodus from Egypt and the crossing of the Red Sea, with Miriam (the prophetess), the sister of Moses and Aaron, at their head... It was not possible in a desert place like this for the Hebrew women to find a number of timbrels enough for thousands of girls, but it is certain and true that they found symbolic timbrels, these of which we speak, which is the practice of piety for many years].

6.4.0.en: Thirteenth: As the Lord builds His new temple He opens the doors of work to all, for He says: “And they that are far off shall come and build in the temple of the LORD” [15], pointing to the Gentiles who were far off and strangers, who have become by their new life in the Lord a spiritual building in the new temple.

6.4.1.en: As it came in Isaiah: “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls, and their kings shall minister unto thee... Therefore thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that the wealth of the nations may be brought unto me, and their kings led” (Isa 60:10-11).
